The theme of this year is “Rethinking the Playbook”. Mr He Lifeng, Vice Premier of the State Council, delivered an opening keynote at the Main Summit by video. The various panels collectively rethink whether the financial playbook needs a major update to live in a world where risk is a constant and resilience a necessity that cannot be taken for granted.

items.source_excerpt:
In response to the potential cybersecurity risks associated with future advances in quantum computing, the HKMA launched the Quantum Preparedness Index (QPI)1 in July 2026 to assess the banking sector’s preparedness for the quantum-safe cryptography. Co-developed by the HKMA and HKUST, the Toolkit aims to support banks in translating awareness into concrete actions, driving the sector towards full quantum readiness, that is, a QPI score of 10 by 2030.

The collaboration reflects HKUST’s role in advancing understanding of emerging technologies and their implications for business and society. The next step is to help banks translate that understanding into clear responsibilities, informed priorities and practical plans.

Through our collaboration with HKUST and the industry, the Toolkit provides a common foundation that banks can adapt to their own circumstances.

The Hong Kong Mortgage Corporation Limited (HKMC) announced today (30 October) the successful completion of its fourth infrastructure loan-backed securities (ILBS) issuance (Bauhinia 4). The issuance builds on the HKMC’s aim of developing the ILBS asset class through regular issuances after three prior issuances between 2023 and 2025 through the Bauhinia brand name. These issuances offer professional investors exposure to a diversified portfolio of project and infrastructure debt across various geographies and sectors.

Mr Colin Pou, Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer of the HKMC, said, “The issuance shows the HKMC’s commitment to the infrastructure financing business and its support for Hong Kong’s development into an infrastructure financing hub. The strong demand from new and existing investors on the issued notes demonstrates the market’s growing recognition of the infrastructure asset class.”

Both new and recurring investors displayed strong interest in the Bauhinia 4 issuance. The widespread investor base includes asset manager, corporate, family office, financial institution, hedge fund, insurer, pension fund, private banking, and security firm investors. There is also a rising appetite from bank investors across Asian countries.

items.source_excerpt:
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority announced today (30 October) the results of its survey on residential mortgage loans (RMLs) in negative equity at end-September 2026.

The estimated number of RMLs in negative equity was 3,819 cases at end-September 2026, as compared to 4,356 cases at end-June 2026. These cases were mainly related to bank staff housing loans or RMLs under mortgage insurance programme, which generally have a higher loan-to-value ratio.

It is important to note that the figures derived from this survey relate only to RMLs provided by authorized institutions on the basis of first mortgages and which the reporting institution knows to be in negative equity (i.e. the outstanding loan amount with the reporting institution exceeds the current market value of the mortgaged property). Not included in these figures are RMLs associated with co-financing schemes which would be in negative equity if the second mortgages were taken into account. The extent to which such RMLs are in negative equity is not known because authorized institutions do not maintain records on the outstanding balances of the second mortgages.

The mortgage portfolios of the surveyed authorized institutions represent about 99% of the industry total. The survey results have been extrapolated to estimate the position of the banking sector as a whole.

The aggregate value of RMLs in negative equity decreased to HK$17.3 billion at end-September 2026 compared with HK$19.6 billion at end-June 2026.

Holders of Stock Exchange Trading Rights and Exchange Participants are requested to note that the Securities and Futures Commission has approved amendments to the Rules for the purpose of tightening the relevant order price limit from 9-times rule to 5-times rule for all securities, except for structured products .

The amendments are set out in the Appendix and will come into effect on Monday, 2 November 2026.

The marked-up version of the amendments can also be downloaded from the “ Rule Update - Rules of the Exchange ” section of the HKEX website.

501I. At the end of the random matching period of the Pre-opening Session when automatic order matching is completed, all auction orders which remain wholly or partly unmatched shall be cancelled and deleted from the System automatically except for those at-auction limit orders the specified price of each of which does not deviate 59 times or more from the nominal price at that time. Such at-auction limit orders shall be converted to limit orders at the input specified price and carried forward to the Continuous Trading Session of the same trading day for automatic order matching. The order entry time of such converted limit orders shall be the time the at-auction limit orders were originally entered into the System. If there is no Continuous Trading Session on that trading day for whatever reason, such at-auction limit orders shall be cancelled and deleted from the System at the end of that trading day.

The Hong Kong Mortgage Corporation Limited (HKMC) today (26 October) announced the highlights of its interim results for 2026.

The HKMC and its subsidiaries continued to fulfil their core missions and social objectives, contributing to the steady growth of Hong Kong’s economy amid an increasingly complex and evolving environment. The missions of the HKMC are to promote: the stability of the banking sector, wider home ownership, the development of the local debt market, and the development of the retirement planning market.

Issued corporate debts totalling HK$24.8 billion (1H 2025: HK$23.3 billion), and continued to be one of the most active issuers in the domestic Hong Kong dollar (HKD) corporate bond market

Outstanding balance of debt securities issued was HK$141.5 billion as of 30 June 2026 (31 December 2025: HK$155.2 billion)

In line with its mandate to promote the development of the retirement planning market in Hong Kong, the HKMC is dedicated to advancing its annuity and reverse mortgage businesses, which face increasing sensitivity and volatility of mark-to-market accounting effects.

Accordingly, the annualised return on equity was 7.2% (1H 2025: 6.2%) and the cost-to-income ratio was 11.7% (1H 2025: 14.2%).

Asset Purchase

Acquired HK$2.9 billion of loan assets (1H 2025: HK$2.7 billion)

Purchased HK$115 million of loans (1H 2025: HK$46 million) under the Dedicated 100% Loan Guarantee Schemes (DLGS)

Debt Issuance

Annuity Business
